assertion_analysis.failure_condition: assert period_reads(48) == period_reads(12) fails if watch._span is called once per hour per counter, because a 48 h scheduled period then costs about four times the reads of a 12 h one; the two sides are two independent runs of the code under test with different inputs, and logs/negative_control.log shows the restored per-cut read reddens it (98 against 26, EXIT=1), so it is not self-referential and it does catch the regression it names.

baseline_suite.note: not armed on the reviewed node; its manifest reads 'not armed for this node', so no base-arm suite log exists to reduce.

findings.text: blocking: merging consecutive cuts by listing index at imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:816-831 discards the hourly cuts a scheduled price row needs for its time-of-day rate. When the listing yields no median (every endpoint below the precision floor) and no headline row exists, the rate falls back to watch.price_at at imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:882, whose value moves hour by hour; the merged stretch prices all its hours at the first hour's rate instead. Reproduced read-only with the module's own helpers: a 24 h scheduled render (overrides utc_start 900/utc_end 1700, a narrow-only listing, no headline) returns 7.755 at the landed code against 3.243 under the base per-cut walk -- a 2.4x change, and the change's own commit message and plan section 24 both state every figure is unchanged. The configuration is reachable: the live table /work/projects/imas_gpu/agents/openrouter-prices.json carries hour-varying schedules for deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813, tencent/hy4-preview and tencent/hy3. The live slug the node measured has an empty schedule, so its recorded figures are unaffected and its gate passes.
